doc.title: Bill Goodwin interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 28, 2025

title: Father's radio career, his death and the return to Los Angeles
summary: His father's radio work with Bob Hope and Burns & Allen; the father's death when Bill was 16, family hardship, and dropping out of high school to learn on the L.A. scene with Levey, Lewis and Manne as mentors.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Your father did a lot of announcing and being involved in some comedy shows. Do you recall as a kid hearing his voice on the television? You know doing a Maxwell House commercial or anything like that? What was that experience like?

Well it was actually radio until I was about 10. There really was no commercial TV per se and nobody had television sets, I mean there were very few. And dad was on the radio and he was on every week and was very well known and he would work with either Bob Hope before I was born, and then when I — after he was working with George Burns and Gracie Allen after I was born, and then he went back to work with Bob Hope, you know, when I was around 8 or 9. And I listened all the time. I loved both shows, and the way he worked in the early TV with Burns & Allen too. He was there in just their first season I think with them on television, and then he went back to Bob Hope which was strictly radio, NBC.
You were only around 16 when he passed away, is that correct?
Did that occurrence affect your education or your choice to start working? Or what did it do to the family?

It affected everything because my dad proved that you can take it with you, because he left us not penniless but in dire straits. My mom really had to struggle to get back on her feet so we left where we were living — we lived in Palm Springs, California. And we left there and went back to Los Angeles where we had been up until when I started high school. I got to L.A. and just immediately got on the scene there. I didn’t finish my last semester of high school and ended up dropping out before graduation. But I was hanging out every night and every day just trying to play, learn to play. I had various fortuitous meetings with some people, young musicians my age or slightly older and they kind of took me in and I already — well to go back a little bit I was already — I already knew Stan Levey and I already knew Mel Lewis where I got to know them pretty quickly by getting back to L.A., and Shelly Manne. And they became like my mentors.
